prize_parts.citation: For establishing that liquid-liquid phase separation driven by multivalent weak interactions is a general physical-chemical principle for organizing biomolecules in cells

statement.case_for: After the first round I keep B046 as my preferred configuration, with the same trio, but I have narrowed what I would ask the citation to carry. The achievement I would credit is the demonstration that biomolecules demix into liquid-like condensed phases governed by valency, affinity and saturation concentration: the 2009 P-granule work showed liquid behaviour in a living cell, and the Rosen multivalent signalling-protein work showed the same thermodynamics in a defined in vitro system. That pairing is a concept of molecular organisation, not a method or a product, and it has been independently reproduced and extended into transcription, stress granules, signalling and disordered-protein physical chemistry. The citation now says 'general physical-chemical principle' and 'organizing biomolecules in cells' so it does not claim that every condensate is an equilibrium phase or functionally essential.
statement.case_against: No other member prefers B046 except the chair, and five distinct first choices cannot reach a majority of five, so I take seriously that my case is the earliest of the leading candidates. Aili, Somfai and Zou press, fairly, that the in-cell evidence is uneven and that parts of the field read as cell biology. Pappu and Mittag are left out by the three-person cap, and the Hyman-Brangwynne and Rosen strands are related, not identical. B010 and B011 have already changed what chemists and clinicians can do at scale, and I cannot say that B046 has reached that level. I have not moved because of counts, but I recognise that if the committee judges maturity decisively, B010 is the strongest alternative.

responses.point: Chabes argues that targeted protein degradation turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction, that PROTACs and cereblon glues share one induced-proximity principle, and that approved glue-class drugs and late-stage degrader trials supply the clinical proof.
responses.response: That framing, an event-driven and catalytic mechanism built around a ternary complex, is a real physical-chemical concept, and it is why I keep B010 as my first alternative. My remaining doubt is the one the chair put as a question: a single sentence covering heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues risks stitching two strands together. The citation you propose is the most defensible version I have seen, since it names the shared principle, but it leaves Sakamoto and Ciulli out of a PROTAC story and explains the glue medicines only retrospectively. If the committee accepts one-principle wording and Handa as the third name, I could rank B010 above B011 as an acceptable second choice. I do not yet think it displaces B046 on conceptual novelty, though it clearly wins on maturity.

responses.point: Aili doubts the cellular evidence for B046, while holding that for degraders the test is whether the work changed what chemists and clinicians can do.
responses.response: I accept that test as a legitimate criterion and that B046 does less well on it today. My answer to the cellular-evidence doubt is that the in vitro framework is not in dispute: phase diagrams, valency dependence and saturation concentrations are measured in purified systems by many groups, and in vivo the P-granule liquid behaviour has been reproduced independently. What is contested is which condensates are phase-separated and functional, and the citation no longer asserts that. I agree with your own caveat that no PROTAC is yet approved, which is a point where B010 and B046 are not so far apart in demonstrated cellular or clinical function as the support counts suggest.

responses.point: Somfai rates Buchwald-Hartwig amination (B035) as the clearest case of a new chemical reaction that became routine, but less novel as a concept than degradation or sequencing, and notes that Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor.
responses.response: I agree that B035 is mature and cleanly attributed, and your own concession that it is less conceptually novel than B010 or B011 is the reason I do not prefer it. Ligand-controlled mechanism is real physical organic and organometallic chemistry, but it extends the logic of the 2010 prize, and Kosugi would need careful handling. For my own preference I put a new principle of organisation ahead of a better method, though I recognise that is a values judgement and not a scientific proof. If the committee sets maturity above novelty, B035 is a more defensible choice than B002 or B013, and I could accept it.

responses.point: Zou presses that B046 is not tied to a chemically established structure, and prefers molecular-sieve design (B002) as a case where structure determining function is proven from synthesis through crystallography to catalysis.
responses.response: I agree that B002 has structural proof and deployment that B046 lacks, and I appreciate that you disclosed your overlap. My reply is that in B046 the quantity that is established is the thermodynamic description, with a phase boundary, a critical concentration and a valency dependence, which is a chemical structure-function statement of a different kind. I would not claim that the molecular structure of a condensate is known. I do share your point that the citation must be narrow, and I share the maturity doubt about another porous-materials award soon after the 2025 MOF prize, so on that point I would rank B002 below B010 and B011 for me.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, prefers B046 with the identical trio and a citation stressing that multivalent weak interactions organize the interior of living cells, and accepts that the physiological claims are unsettled.
responses.response: I asked you in round one what wording would survive the criticism, and I now suggest we align on a citation that credits the principle and the demonstrated liquid behaviour, without 'organizes the interior of living cells' as an unqualified claim. I am more conservative on the cellular statement than your wording. I also want us to be candid that two supporters is not enough; I will not trade my scientific judgment for a majority, but I will rank B010 and B011 as acceptable if the comparison on maturity goes against us. I would be interested in whether you would accept a trio change to include Pappu if that helps with the physical-chemistry framing, although I would keep Rosen because the multivalent in vitro work is the quantitative anchor.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will credit the in vitro thermodynamic framework or the claim that condensates organise living cells, and whether the narrowed citation satisfies colleagues who see this as cell biology.
Whether Pappu or Mittag should displace Rosen or either of the cell-based pair; I keep Rosen but the choice is not settled.
Whether B010 can be covered by one honest sentence and whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I have not checked clinical status, which is from general knowledge, not the supplied files.
The late-stage status of degraders and the approval status of glue-class medicines are unverified in these materials.
statement.conflict_note: No change: my research on lipid and protein self-assembly is scientifically close to B046 and B051, which I am not placing in the preferred configuration, and I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited candidate. I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, an institutional overlap, and not a recusal ground. I have declared the scientific closeness to B046 openly, and I leave it to the chair and committee to judge whether it affects my vote.
